title: Summer Software Builders Kickoff
description: Start the season with local developers sharing what they are building, the technical problems they are exploring, and the skills they hope to sharpen over the next few months.

title: React Server Components in Practice
description: Walk through practical patterns for deciding what belongs on the server, what stays interactive on the client, and how those choices affect performance and maintainability.

title: Designing a Full Stack Feature from End to End
description: Follow one product feature from interface design through API boundaries, persistence, testing, and deployment while discussing the tradeoffs made at each layer.

title: TypeScript APIs That Explain Themselves
description: Explore discriminated unions, branded values, and focused utility types that make application contracts easier to understand without turning the type system into a puzzle.

title: Finding the Smallest Useful Version of an Idea
description: Founders and builders will practice reducing ambitious concepts into focused experiments that can reveal genuine customer interest before a team commits months of work.

title: Cloud Cost Signals Every Team Should Watch
description: Learn how to connect infrastructure spending with application behavior using practical dashboards, budgets, and ownership habits that teams can maintain over time.

title: Evaluating AI Features Beyond the Demo
description: Discuss repeatable evaluation sets, failure analysis, latency, and cost so that promising AI prototypes can become dependable features for real users.

title: Maintainer Office Hours: Issues, Reviews, and Releases
description: Bring questions about triage, pull request review, contributor communication, and release planning for a collaborative session with experienced open source maintainers.

title: Building Influence Without a Management Title
description: Explore practical ways to create clarity, support teammates, advocate for good decisions, and grow technical influence from any role on a team.

title: Live Portfolio Review for Early-Career Developers
description: Volunteers will review project portfolios and offer concrete feedback on storytelling, technical depth, visual presentation, and the details hiring teams tend to notice.

title: Reliable Background Jobs and Queues
description: Examine retries, idempotency, scheduling, observability, and failure recovery for background work that must remain trustworthy under real production conditions.

title: Design Tokens from Figma to Production
description: Connect visual decisions to maintainable frontend code by exploring token naming, theming, component APIs, and collaboration between designers and engineers.

title: Testing Strategies for Teams That Ship Often
description: Compare unit, integration, contract, and browser tests to find a balanced approach that catches meaningful regressions without making every change painfully slow.

title: A Practical React Performance Clinic
description: Diagnose representative rendering problems and learn when memoization, state restructuring, code splitting, or simpler component boundaries provide the biggest improvement.

title: Authentication Across the Modern Web Stack
description: Trace sessions, cookies, authorization, and account recovery across browser, server, and database layers with an emphasis on secure defaults and understandable code.

title: Runtime Validation Meets Static Types
description: See how teams can keep external data honest by pairing TypeScript with runtime schemas at API, form, configuration, and persistence boundaries.

title: Customer Interviews That Change the Roadmap
description: Practice asking neutral questions, recognizing recurring pain, and translating interview evidence into product decisions without simply collecting feature requests.

title: Making Deployments Boring Again
description: Review deployment safeguards, progressive delivery, rollback design, and observability practices that turn releases from stressful events into routine operations.

title: Data Pipelines You Can Debug at 2 AM
description: Explore lineage, validation, replayability, and observability patterns that make production data pipelines easier to understand when something inevitably goes wrong.

title: Welcoming New Contributors Without Burning Out Maintainers
description: Share sustainable approaches to documentation, issue labeling, mentorship, automation, and boundaries that help open source communities welcome people well.

title: Technical Stories and Intentional Networking
description: Build confidence introducing your work, describing your impact, and creating professional connections that feel genuine rather than transactional.

title: Technical Interview Practice Lab
description: Work through approachable coding, debugging, and system-thinking exercises in small groups with an emphasis on communication and constructive feedback.

title: PostgreSQL Indexes Without the Mystery
description: Learn how common index types work, how query plans reveal useful clues, and why an index can sometimes cost more than it saves.

title: Accessible Interfaces Beyond the Checklist
description: Use real interaction examples to examine keyboard flow, focus management, content clarity, assistive technology, and accessibility as an ongoing design practice.

title: Reading Production Systems Through Their Signals
description: Bring logs, metrics, traces, and user reports together to form better hypotheses and shorten the path from a vague incident to a useful diagnosis.

title: Forms That Stay Manageable as Products Grow
description: Discuss validation, field state, async behavior, accessibility, and component boundaries for complex React forms that must evolve without becoming fragile.

title: Monoliths, Services, and the Cost of Boundaries
description: Compare modular monoliths and distributed services through team ownership, deployment, data consistency, and operational complexity rather than architecture fashion.

title: Building a Type-Safe Developer Tool
description: Explore command parsing, configuration schemas, error design, and packaging while building a small TypeScript tool intended for other developers to use.

title: Startup Runway and Responsible Growth
description: Learn how early-stage teams can reason about runway, hiring, pricing, and growth investments while keeping financial assumptions visible and adaptable.

title: Infrastructure as Code Review Workshop
description: Review realistic infrastructure changes for security, recoverability, naming, ownership, and operational clarity while developing a practical team checklist.

title: Retrieval Systems for Useful AI Answers
description: Examine chunking, embedding, retrieval, ranking, citation, and evaluation choices that shape whether an AI assistant can answer from trusted information.

title: Documentation People Can Actually Navigate
description: Improve project documentation by organizing around reader goals, adding runnable examples, clarifying contribution paths, and maintaining information as code changes.

title: Negotiating Scope, Support, and Compensation
description: Prepare for career conversations by gathering evidence, defining priorities, asking clear questions, and understanding the full range of outcomes available.

title: Debugging Horror Stories and What They Taught Us
description: A Halloween-friendly collection of mysterious bugs, misleading symptoms, and practical lessons about staying systematic when software behaves impossibly.

title: Versioning APIs Without Surprising Consumers
description: Discuss compatibility, deprecation, schema evolution, migration support, and communication patterns for APIs that serve multiple clients and teams.

title: Testing a Product Before It Is Fully Built
description: Use prototypes, task scenarios, and lightweight interviews to learn where an experience succeeds or fails before implementation becomes expensive to change.

title: Threat Modeling for Everyday Product Teams
description: Practice identifying assets, trust boundaries, likely abuse cases, and proportionate mitigations without requiring every engineer to become a security specialist.

title: State Management Decision Clinic
description: Compare local state, context, URL state, server-state libraries, and shared stores by working through realistic product requirements and failure modes.

title: Graceful Failure Across the Stack
description: Design useful failure behavior across interfaces, APIs, workers, and databases so that partial outages remain understandable and recoverable for users and operators.

title: Refactoring Legacy JavaScript with TypeScript
description: Plan an incremental migration that improves confidence early, avoids a risky rewrite, and uses newly discovered type information to guide design improvements.

title: Founder Lessons from the Year
description: Local founders will share the experiments, difficult decisions, unexpected wins, and changed assumptions that shaped their companies throughout 2026.

title: Incident Reviews That Lead to Better Systems
description: Learn how blameless review, clear timelines, contributing factors, and owned follow-up work can turn production incidents into durable operational improvements.

title: Communicating Data Findings with Honesty
description: Present uncertainty, limitations, context, and actionable conclusions in ways that help decision-makers understand what the data supports and what it does not.

title: Open Source Project Showcase 2026
description: Contributors will demonstrate projects they improved this year, explain their contributions, and share what they learned from working in public with distributed teams.

title: Creating a Personal Mentorship Map
description: Identify the different kinds of guidance, sponsorship, peer support, and community connection that can help sustain a healthy long-term career.

title: Planning Your 2027 Developer Learning Path
description: Turn broad ambitions into a realistic learning plan with focused projects, feedback loops, milestones, and enough flexibility to adapt as interests change.

title: Backend Engineering Lessons from 2026
description: Reflect on the database, API, reliability, and distributed-systems lessons that mattered this year and the practices worth carrying into future projects.

title: Interface Design Retrospective and Showcase
description: Designers and frontend developers will share work from the year, explain the decisions behind it, and reflect on what they would approach differently now.

title: Year-End Developer Community Social
description: Close out the year with relaxed conversation, project demos, favorite technical discoveries, and new connections across the Bloomington-Normal developer community.

title: Holiday Open Source Co-Working Session
description: Drop in for a quiet, friendly online session to improve documentation, review a pull request, fix a small issue, or simply spend time building alongside others.
